---
title: "Accessing the data"
output: rmarkdown::html_document
---

Use the R functions for the package's documented output tables, export those
tables for use in other software, or read the published Parquet files directly.
`swelections` is an R package; it does not currently provide separate Python,
Stata or SPSS packages.

## Source selection in R

The `source` argument controls how data are obtained. For most users, keep the
default `"auto"`; choose another source explicitly when you need a particular input:

- `"auto"` (default) selects approved canonical data for the requested election
  and function, otherwise a supported remote source. It never selects local raw
  files. If neither source is supported, the request gives an error.
- `"canonical"` explicitly reads the package's validated, published historical
  data, without raw-source fallback.
- `"remote"` reads a current, official and explicitly supported Swedish Election
  Authority source, even when canonical data exist. It does not fall back to
  canonical or local data.
- `"local"` reads your own compatible saved raw archive, selected explicitly
  with `data_dir`.

Remote formats and coverage vary between elections and functions. A new
presentation file does not automatically replace a withdrawn detailed export.
See [Coverage](coverage.html) for availability and `data_sources` for detailed
source requirements. [Get started](swelections.html) shows the R interface.

## Exporting tables

After retrieving a table in R, you can export it for use in other software.
CSV is a general import option. The separate R package `haven` can write Stata
`.dta` and SPSS `.sav` files:

```r
results_table <- results(year = 2022, election = "parliamentary", level = "national")
export_table <- results_table[, c("election_year", "party_code", "party_designation",
                                  "votes", "vote_share")]
write.csv(export_table, "results.csv", row.names = FALSE, na = "")

# Requires install.packages("haven")
haven::write_dta(export_table, "results.dta")
haven::write_sav(export_table, "results.sav")
```

The example selects a few columns for export. Stata variable names are limited
to 32 characters; some full swelections column names exceed that limit.

These are file exports, not separate swelections interfaces. Preserve identifiers
as text and check how the receiving program imports missing values. A CSV file
does not retain all R column types; do not replace missing values with zero.

## Published Parquet files

The [data-v0.4.1 release](https://github.com/richardohrvall/swelections/releases/tag/data-v0.4.1)
contains 200 Parquet files and 16 product manifests. A manifest identifies the
filenames, schema, sizes, SHA256 checksums and source provenance. Use the data
generation documented for your package version.

Some files contain several stored tables or geographic levels; other public
views require joins across files. Directly reading a file therefore need not
reproduce a complete `results()` call. Consult the manifest rather than combining
all rows or files indiscriminately.

## Reading a Parquet file in Python

Install `pandas` and a Parquet engine such as `pyarrow` in your Python environment.
This example reads the published Falun 2019 re-election file directly. The
manifest is used for file verification: the byte count and SHA256 must match
before the data are read. The municipality filter then selects one geographic
level. This is direct file access, not a Python API provided by `swelections`.

```python
import hashlib
import io
import json
from urllib.request import urlopen

import pandas as pd

base = "https://github.com/richardohrvall/swelections/releases/download/data-v0.4.1"
with urlopen(f"{base}/rkl2019-re-election-manifest.json") as response:
    manifest = json.load(response)

# This example targets the documented v0.4.1 storage contract.
assert manifest["schema_version"] == 3
asset = next(
    item for item in manifest["assets"]
    if item["file"] == "rkl2019-re-election-kf-2080-results-final.parquet"
)
with urlopen(f"{base}/{asset['file']}") as response:
    payload = response.read()

assert len(payload) == asset["bytes"]
assert hashlib.sha256(payload).hexdigest() == asset["sha256"]

tables = pd.read_parquet(io.BytesIO(payload), engine="pyarrow")
municipality = tables.loc[tables[".table"].eq("municipality")]
print(municipality[["municipality_name", "party_abbreviation", "votes"]])
```

The file also contains district rows. Its `.table` column distinguishes the
stored views; other files may use `.component` or additional selectors. Check
the manifest's `tables` entries and declared columns rather than assuming every
file has the same layout.

Retain the data-release identifier with your analysis. For technical category
and storage definitions, see the [value/storage contract](https://github.com/richardohrvall/swelections/blob/main/development/VALUE_CONTRACT.md).

## Complementary SCB statistics

Statistics Sweden's aggregate statistics can also be retrieved programmatically
through its [PxWeb API](https://www.scb.se/en/services/open-data-api/), for example
with the R package [pxweb](https://ropengov.github.io/pxweb/). This is a separate,
complementary resource, not a swelections interface. See
[Sources & methodology](sources-methodology.html#related-official-statistics)
for relevant statistics and the distinction between aggregates and restricted
microdata.
